topic: Promo: one topic line in, one finished animated video out, and what the buyer gets
title: ONE LINE IN
ONE VIDEO OUT

script.text: One animated video can feel like a full time job. Writing it. Recording it. Cutting it. Adding sound. Exporting it. Then doing it all again tomorrow.
Now try this. Type one line. What if you could see one minute ahead?

script.beat: 3 stages: script, voice, shot list, storyboard
script.text: The pipeline writes the script. Records the voice. Cuts a shot list on every word. Then draws a storyboard you can check before anything renders.
Every frame is animated in code. The sound is built to match. And the audio is mastered to minus fourteen LUFS.

script.beat: 6 what you get and what you bring
script.text: You get the full system: the engine, the cast, seven sets, the scripts, and the guides that tie it together. You bring your own ElevenLabs and Claude access. No keys come inside.
One line in. One finished video out. Get the full system. Link in the description.

science.claim: Making one animated video can feel like a full time job.
science.working: Opinion, not a statistic: no figure is stated or implied. Kept as a feeling, not a number.

science.claim: One topic line in, one finished animated video out.
science.working: The pipeline takes a topic line and produces a mastered video: script, voice, shot list, storyboard, animation, sound, master.
science.source: skill brief SKILL.md, description and section 3

science.claim: The pipeline cuts a shot list on every word, and a cut lands two frames before its cue word.
science.working: plan.py resolves each edit cue against word timings; lead defaults to 2 frames (LEAD = ep.get('lead', 2)).

science.claim: A storyboard is checked before anything renders.
science.working: Steps 4 and 5 (stills, then the look self-check) come before the video render; the brief says no video render until the stills pass.

science.claim: Every frame is animated in code.
science.working: Each shot is a React/SVG component, a pure function of its clock t, rendered by Remotion.

science.claim: The sound is built to match: effects are cued to shots and words.
science.working: sound.events use cues such as S3+2 or a word; sfx.py resolves them to frames.

science.claim: The audio is mastered to minus fourteen LUFS, true peak under minus one dBTP.
science.working: master.py brings the mix to -14 LUFS integrated, true peak -1 dBTP (loudnorm).
src/engine/index.ts exports: study, stairwell, classroom, rooftop, kitchen, schematic, bedroom = 7. Re-count before publishing if sets are added.

science.claim: The system includes the engine, the cast, the scripts and the guides.
science.working: engine/ (rig, props, light, room, ui), cast = LOOKS (pip, pipHood, pipInk, mo, sis, mom, suit), scripts/ (voice, plan, stills, board, sfx, mixcheck, master), references/ (formula, look, kit, sound, traps).
science.source: bundle contents; SKILL.md section 1 and Where an episode lives

science.claim: Buyers bring their own ElevenLabs and Claude access; no keys are bundled.
science.working: The brief forbids bundling anyone's API key; keys are read from the environment or a .env by name only.

science.claim: The clip shown is a real episode.
science.working: S24 to S27 are shots 15, 16, 17 and 11 of src/episodes/glimpse60/shots.tsx, drawn by this engine.
